lessons.title: The Map of Pakistan and Our Flag
lessons.notes_html:
Our Country

  • Pakistan has four provinces: Balochistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab and Sindh.
  • The federal areas are Azad Jammu and Kashmir, Gilgit Baltistan and Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT).
  • The capital of Pakistan is Islamabad.
  • Balochistan is the largest province by area, and Punjab is the largest province by population.
  • Gilgit Baltistan is situated in the north of Pakistan.

Solved Questions and Answers

Q: Look at the map of Pakistan carefully and write the names of four provinces and federal areas.

Ans: The four provinces of Pakistan are Balochistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab and Sindh. The federal areas are Azad Jammu and Kashmir, Gilgit Baltistan and Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT).

Q: Draw/Make the flag of Pakistan in your notebook under the guidance of your teacher and colour it. Point out the colours representing the Muslim and other religions.

Ans: Note: Drawing and colouring the flag is a practical activity and has no written answer. The colours are: the green colour stands for the Muslims, and the white colour represents the people of other religions. The Moon (Crescent) is the symbol of progress and the star is the symbol of light and knowledge (learning).

Q: Collect the pictures showing the culture of different areas of Pakistan in group, show it to your class mates and discuss them among yourselves.

Ans: Note: This is a group collection and discussion activity in the book and has no written answer.

Q: In the guidance of your teachers, trace the following given provinces on a chart paper in group and make their cut outs. Now combine these cut outs and complete the map of Pakistan from it. (Punjab, Sindh, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Balochistan, Azad Jammu and Kashmir, Gilgit Baltistan)

Ans: Note: This is a practical tracing and cut-out activity in the book and has no written answer.

Key Points

  • Pakistan has four provinces and three federal areas.
  • Our flag has two colours: green for the Muslims and white for the people of other religions.
  • The crescent means progress and the star means light and knowledge.

mcqs.q: How many provinces are there in Pakistan?
mcqs.why: Pakistan has four provinces: Balochistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab and Sindh.

mcqs.why: The Moon (Crescent) in the flag of Pakistan is the symbol of progress.

mcqs.why: The star in the flag of Pakistan is the symbol of light and knowledge (learning).

mcqs.why: Muzaffarabad is the capital of Azad Jammu and Kashmir.

mcqs.q: Which province is the largest by population?
mcqs.why: Punjab is the largest province of Pakistan according to its population.

mcqs.q: Gilgit Baltistan is situated in which part of Pakistan?
mcqs.why: Gilgit Baltistan is situated in the North of Pakistan.

lessons.title: End of Chapter Exercise
lessons.notes_html:
What We Learned

  • Pakistan came into being on 14th August 1947.
  • People speak different languages in different provinces, and their dress and food are also different.

Solved Questions and Answers

Q: Exercise Q1 (MCQ): When did Pakistan come into being?

Ans: 14th August 1947. (The other options in the book were 23rd March 1940 and 11th September 1948.)

Q: Exercise Q1 (MCQ): How many provinces are there in Pakistan?

Ans: Four.

Q: Exercise Q1 (MCQ): How many colours are there in the flag of Pakistan?

Ans: Two.

Q: Exercise Q2 (True/False): The green colour in Pakistan Flag points out to the other religions.

Ans: False — The green colour stands for the Muslims; the white colour represents the people of other religions.

Q: Exercise Q2 (True/False): The capital of Azad Jammu and Kashmir is Muzaffarabad.

Ans: True.

Q: Exercise Q2 (True/False): Balochistan is the smallest province according to its area.

Ans: False — Balochistan is the largest province on the basis of territory (area).

Q: Exercise Q2 (True/False): Punjab is the largest province of Pakistan according to its population.

Ans: True.

Q: Exercise Q2 (True/False): Gilgit Baltistan is located in the South of Pakistan.

Ans: False — Gilgit Baltistan is situated in the North of Pakistan.

Q: Q3. What is the name of the capital of Pakistan?

Ans: The capital of Pakistan is Islamabad.

Q: Q4. Write down the difference between the culture of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Sindh — Language.

Ans: In Sindh the people speak Sindhi language. In Khyber Pakhtunkhwa the people speak Pashto, Hindku, Saraiki and Chitrali.

Q: Q4. Write down the difference between the culture of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Sindh — Dress.

Ans: In Sindh the people wear Shilwar Qameez, Ajrak (Sindhi Shawl) and Sindhi Cap. In Khyber Pakhtunkhwa men wear Shilwar Qameez, Turban, Chitrali Cap, Qaraquli Cap (Jinnah Cap) and Peshawari Chappal, and ladies wear Shilwar Qameez with embroidery.

Q: Q4. Write down the difference between the culture of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Sindh — Food.

Ans: In Sindh the people love to eat rice, koki (special Sindhi bread) and spinach. In Khyber Pakhtunkhwa the famous foods are Pulao, Chapli Kabab and green tea.

Key Points

  • Pakistan came into being on 14th August 1947.
  • The people of Sindh speak Sindhi; the people of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa speak Pashto, Hindku, Saraiki and Chitrali.
  • Ajrak and Sindhi Cap are worn in Sindh; Chapli Kabab and Pulao are famous foods of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

mcqs.why: In Sindh the people love to eat rice, koki (special Sindhi bread) and spinach.

lessons.title: Village and City Life
lessons.notes_html:
Village and City

  • In a village, houses are open and made of mud, and people do farming.
  • The environment of a village is neat and clean, but there are less facilities of health and education.
  • In a city there are tall and well-constructed buildings and offices.
  • Cities have the best facilities of health and education, but their environment is not clean due to factories and the noise of traffic.

Solved Questions and Answers

Q: The children in group compare the characteristics of both the village and city from the pictures.

Ans: Note: This is a group discussion activity in the book. From the pictures: life in a village has mud houses and farming, while life in a city has tall buildings and offices. Village houses are open and made of mud and the environment is neat and clean, but there are less facilities of health and education. Cities have tall and well-constructed buildings and the best facilities of health and education, but their environment is not clean due to factories and the noise of traffic.

Q: Activity (book p. 17): The Children in pairs tell about their favourite place (city or village) and also tell two reasons of it.

Ans: Note: This is a practical/oral activity in the book and has no written answer.

Key Points

  • Villages have mud houses, farming and fresh air.
  • Cities have tall buildings, wide roads and the best facilities of health and education.

mcqs.q: Houses in a village are mostly made of what?
mcqs.why: Village houses are open and made of mud, and the environment of the village is neat and clean.

mcqs.q: Where do we see tall buildings and offices?
mcqs.why: Life in a city has tall and well-constructed buildings and offices.

mcqs.q: The environment of a village is what?
mcqs.why: Village houses are open and made of mud and the environment is neat and clean.

mcqs.q: Why is the environment of a city not clean?
options: Because of factories and the noise of traffic
mcqs.why: The environment of cities is not clean due to factories and the noise of traffic.

mcqs.q: Where are the best facilities of health and education?
mcqs.why: Cities have tall buildings and the best facilities of health and education.

mcqs.q: Fresh air is found in which place?
mcqs.why: Fresh air is found in a village, where there are fields and open places.

mcqs.q: A farmer works mostly in which place?
mcqs.why: A farmer grows crops in the fields of a village.

mcqs.q: Streams and wells are found in which place?
mcqs.why: Streams and wells are found in villages, from where people get water.

mcqs.q: An airport is found in which place?
mcqs.why: An airport is found in a city. Big facilities like airports are in cities.

mcqs.q: Wide roads are found in which place?
mcqs.why: Wide roads are found in cities, where there is much traffic.

People Who Help Us

Q: Which profession will you adopt when you grow-up and why?

Ans: I will become a doctor when I grow up. A doctor treats sick people and helps them become healthy again.

Q: Write any three facilities that are available in the city and not in the village.

Ans: Three facilities available in the city are: (1) a university for higher education, (2) an airport, and (3) the best facilities of health and education. The book says the best facilities of health and education are available in the cities.

Q: Which facility will you provide in a village first and why?

Ans: I will provide a hospital in the village first. The book says there are less facilities of health in villages, so sick people in the village need a hospital for their treatment.

Key Points

  • A butcher sells meat, a cobbler mends shoes, a tailor stitches clothes and a doctor treats sick people.
  • A hospital is the first facility a village needs, because villages have less health facilities.

Q: Activity (book p. 23): Role Play — Divide the children in groups. In each group a child becomes a government officer and another to play the role of a citizen. Ask every group to tell the duties of government and rights of the citizens in the given time by playing the role.

lessons.title: End of Chapter Exercise
lessons.notes_html:
Rights and Duties of Citizens

  • Two rights of the citizens are: clean water for drinking and the provision of electricity, and freedom to adopt a profession.
  • Two duties of the citizens are: to abide by the law, and careful use of water and electricity and avoid wasting them.
  • The police department takes care of the people and their property. Police stations are made to control crimes.

Solved Questions and Answers

Q: Few facilities are noted down. Tick the facility available in your locality. (Hospital, Airport, Police Station, School, Park, Facility of Clean Water, Courts, Post Office)

Ans: This depends on the child's own locality, so every child ticks the facilities found near his or her home. For example, a school, a hospital, a police station, a park, the facility of clean water, courts and a post office are ticked where they are present. An airport is found only in big cities.

Q: Write down the two important public issues of your locality.

Ans: This answer is different for every locality, and children write the problems of their own area. For example: (i) shortage of clean drinking water, (ii) broken and dirty roads.

Q: Write any two rights and two duties of the citizens.

Ans: Two rights of the citizens are: (1) clean water for drinking and the provision of electricity, (2) freedom to adopt a profession. Two duties of the citizens are: (1) to abide by the law, (2) careful use of water and electricity and avoid wasting them.

Q: Which department take care of the people and their property?

Ans: The police department takes care of the people and their property. The book says police stations are made to control crimes.

Key Points

  • Rights are what citizens should get; duties are what citizens should do.
  • The police take care of the people and their property.

mcqs.why: Clean water for drinking and the provision of electricity are the rights of the citizens.

mcqs.q: To abide by the law is what of the citizens?
mcqs.why: To abide by the law is a duty of the citizens. Every citizen must follow the law.

mcqs.q: Which department takes care of the people and their property?
mcqs.why: The police department takes care of the people and their property.

mcqs.why: Police stations are made to control crimes and to protect the people.

mcqs.why: Careful use of water and electricity and avoiding wasting them is a duty of the citizens.

mcqs.why: Freedom to adopt a profession is a right of the citizens.

mcqs.why: An airport is found only in big cities; other facilities like schools and hospitals are found in many localities.

mcqs.why: Shortage of clean drinking water and broken and dirty roads are public issues of a locality.

mcqs.q: Which facility treats sick people in a locality?
mcqs.why: A hospital is the facility where sick people are treated.

mcqs.q: Wasting water and electricity is what?
mcqs.why: It is our duty to use water and electricity carefully and avoid wasting them.

lessons.title: End of Chapter Exercise
lessons.notes_html:
Festivals

  • Muslims celebrate Eid-ul-Fitr on the first day of Shawal, after Ramzan-ul-Mubarak.
  • Eid-ul-Azha is celebrated in the memory of the sacrifice of Hazrat Ibrahim and Hazrat Ismail.
  • Festivals of other religions are Christmas, Holi, Diwali and Baisakhi.

Solved Questions and Answers

Q: How do the muslims celebrate Eid-ul-Fitr?

Ans: Muslims celebrate Eid-ul-Fitr on the first day of Shawal, after the completion of Ramzan-ul-Mubarak. On this day they meet and congratulate their relatives and friends. After offering their Salah of Eid, they go to their houses and give Eidi to the children. Sadqa-e-Fitr is given to the poor Muslims to include them in the Eid celebration.

Q: In whose memory Eid-ul-Azha is celebrated?

Ans: Eid-ul-Azha is celebrated in the memory of the sacrifice of Hazrat Ibrahim and Hazrat Ismail.

Q: Name any two of the festivals of other religions.

Ans: Two festivals of other religions are Christmas and Holi. The book also names Diwali and Baisakhi.

Q: Read the following words and write the name of festival in box: Hazrat Ibrahim, 10th Dhul Hijjah, Sacrifice

Ans: Eid-ul-Azha

Q: Read the following words and write the name of festival in box: Moon, Fitrana, Eidi

Ans: Eid-ul-Fitr

Q: Read the following words and write the name of festival in box: Soam, Aftaar, Sacred Month

Ans: Ramzan-ul-Mubarak

Q: Read the following words and write the name of festival in box: December, Jesus, Christians

Ans: Christmas

Q: Read the following words and write the name of festival in box: Hindus, Colours, Spring

Ans: Holi

Q: Read the following words and write the name of festival in box: The first day of year, Sikh, Joys

Ans: Baisakhi

Key Points

  • Eid-ul-Fitr comes on the first day of Shawal after Ramzan.
  • Eid-ul-Azha is on 10th Dhul Hijjah in the memory of the sacrifice of Hazrat Ibrahim and Hazrat Ismail.

mcqs.why: Eid-ul-Azha is celebrated in the memory of the sacrifice of Hazrat Ibrahim and Hazrat Ismail.

mcqs.why: The words of Eid-ul-Azha in the book are: Hazrat Ibrahim, 10th Dhul Hijjah, Sacrifice.

mcqs.why: The words of Christmas in the book are: December, Jesus, Christians.

mcqs.why: The words of Holi in the book are: Hindus, Colours, Spring.

lessons.title: Living Things and Materials Around Us
lessons.notes_html:
Living and Non-Living Things

  • Living things grow, reproduce and move, and they need air, food and water for living.
  • A bus or a car only moves; it does not grow and does not reproduce, so it is a non-living thing.

Natural Resources and Materials

  • The natural resources named in the book are land, water, air and sun.
  • Objects made by people from natural resources, such as pots, taps and jewellery, are man-made objects.
  • Soil is used for farming and growing crops; we build houses on land, and pots are made of clay (soil).
  • Wood is used for furniture and paper. We get wood from forests.
  • Iron is used for taps, hand pumps and ceiling fans.
  • Glass is made of sand, and sand is got from the land. Paper is made of wood.

Solved Questions and Answers

Q: Bus or a car moves from one place to another. Are they living things? Tell the reason of your answer.

Ans: No, a bus or a car is not a living thing. Living things grow, reproduce and move, and they need air, food and water for living. A bus or car only moves; it does not grow and does not reproduce, so it is a non-living thing.

Q: Activity (book p. 32): Divide the children in two groups, and specify a part of school to each group. Ask one group to make a list of living things and other group to make a list of non-living things and then ask them to discuss among themselves.

Ans: Note: This is a practical/oral activity in the book and has no written answer.

Q: Activity (book p. 34): Look at the following pictures carefully and tell your class how air is used in these pictures.

Ans: Note: This is an oral activity in the book and has no written answer. In the pictures, moving air (wind) turns the windmill, and air fills the parachute and helps it come down slowly and safely.

Q: Activity (book p. 35): (Group-work) Make a list of the available natural resources and man-made objects in your school.

Ans: Note: This is a group-work activity in the book and has no fixed written answer. The book names land, water, air and sun as natural resources. Objects made by people from natural resources, such as pots, taps and jewellery, are man-made objects.

Q: Write the use of the following material objects: Soil

Ans: 1. Soil (land) is used for farming and growing crops. 2. We build houses on land. 3. Pots are made of clay (soil).

Q: Write the use of the following material objects: Wood

Ans: 1. Furniture, such as the cabinet shown in the exercise, is made of wood. 2. Paper is made of wood. 3. We get wood from forests and people make different things from it for our daily use.

Q: Write the use of the following material objects: Iron

Ans: 1. Taps are made of iron. 2. Hand pumps are made of iron. 3. The ceiling fan shown in the exercise is made of iron.

Q: What is glass made of?

Ans: Glass is made of sand. Sand is got from the land.

Q: What is paper made of?

Ans: Paper is made of wood. Wood is got from trees in the forests.

Key Points

  • Living things grow and reproduce; non-living things do not.
  • Land, water, air and sun are natural resources.
  • Glass is made of sand, paper is made of wood, and taps and fans are made of iron.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a living thing?
mcqs.why: A tree is a living thing. Living things grow, reproduce and move, and they need air, food and water.

mcqs.q: A bus is a non-living thing because it does not do what?
mcqs.why: A bus or car only moves; it does not grow and does not reproduce, so it is a non-living thing.

mcqs.q: Living things need air, food and what for living?
mcqs.why: Living things need air, food and water for living. Without them they cannot live.

mcqs.q: Glass is made of what?
mcqs.why: Glass is made of sand. Sand is got from the land.

mcqs.q: Paper is made of what?
mcqs.why: Paper is made of wood. Wood is got from trees in the forests.

mcqs.q: Pots are made of what?
mcqs.why: Pots are made of clay, which is soil. Soil is also used for farming and growing crops.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a man-made object?
mcqs.why: Objects made by people from natural resources, such as pots, taps and jewellery, are man-made objects.

mcqs.q: Moving air is called what?
mcqs.why: Moving air (wind) turns the windmill, as shown in the pictures in the book.

mcqs.q: A parachute comes down slowly and safely because it is filled with what?
mcqs.why: Air fills the parachute and helps it come down slowly and safely.

mcqs.q: Furniture, like a cabinet, is made of what?
mcqs.why: Furniture, such as the cabinet shown in the exercise, is made of wood. Paper is also made of wood.

lessons.title: Why Water Is Important
lessons.notes_html:
Water Is Life

  • Water is very important for all living things. Living things cannot live without water, so water is the sign of life.
  • The areas named in the book where there is shortage of water are Tharparker, Badin, Dadu and Chaghi, because there is no rain and there is less water there.

Solved Questions and Answers

Q: Why water is necessary for living things?

Ans: Water is very important for all the living things. Living things cannot live without water, so water is the sign of life.

Q: Activity (book p. 43): Make posters with the help of your teacher to show the importance of careful use of water.

Ans: Note: This is a practical activity in the book and has no written answer.

Q: Activity (book p. 45): Find out the areas where there is shortage of water with the help of your parents.

Ans: Note: This is a find-out activity in the book and has no fixed written answer. The book names Tharparker, Badin, Dadu and Chaghi as areas where there is shortage of water, because there is no rain and there is less water there.

Key Points

  • Water is the sign of life; no living thing can live without water.
  • Tharparker, Badin, Dadu and Chaghi have shortage of water.

mcqs.why: Water is very important for all living things. Living things cannot live without water, so water is the sign of life.

lessons.title: Leaves, Roots and Fruits
lessons.notes_html:
How a Plant Grows

  • A plant kept in the courtyard gets light, water and air, so it grows well. A plant kept in a room does not get light, so it does not grow well.

Leaves, Roots and Fruits

  • Leaves are of different shapes: wide, oval, small and oblong.
  • We eat the roots of some plants: beetroot, turnip, carrot and radish.
  • Flowering plants have flowers and seeds in them; non-flowering plants have no flowers and seeds.
  • Fruits are an important part of plants. Fruits with seeds named in the book are apple, mango and watermelon.

Solved Questions and Answers

Q: Activity (book p. 49): Project: Take two flowerpots with plants in it. Keep one flowerpot out in the courtyard where it gets light, water and air, whereas keep the other plant in the room where it does not get light. After every three days, observe both the plants and write the results in the given table.

Ans: Note: This is a practical/oral activity in the book and has no written answer. The plant kept in the courtyard gets light, water and air, so it grows well. The plant kept in the room does not get light, so it does not grow well.

Q: Name the picture: a very big, round leaf with deep cuts in it (first picture). Leaves are of different shapes. Look at the following pictures carefully and name the shapes of leaves with the help of given words. Wide, Oval, Small, Oblong.

Ans: Wide

Q: Name the picture: a big round green leaf with a toothed edge (second picture, top row middle)

Ans: Oval

Q: Name the picture: a single small green leaf with a pointed tip (third picture, top row right)

Ans: Small

Q: Name the picture: a long stem with many long, narrow leaves on both sides (fourth picture, bottom row left)

Ans: Oblong

Q: Name the picture: a small stem with three small leaves (fifth picture, bottom row right)

Ans: Small

Q: Can you name some other roots that are eaten?

Ans: We eat the roots of some plants. The roots named in the book are beetroot, turnip, carrot and radish.

Q: Activity (book p. 50): Collect various types of leaves in group, place them on a chart and fill their outlines with colours.

Ans: Note: This is a practical/oral activity in the book and has no written answer.

Q: Activity (book p. 51): Observe the environment around you to see which are the flowering and non-flowering plants. Write their names with the help of your teacher.

Ans: Note: This is a practical/oral activity in the book and has no written answer. There are flowers and seeds in the flowering plants, whereas there are no flowers and seeds in the non-flowering plants.

Q: Activity (book p. 51): Which one of the fruits do you like?

Ans: Note: This is a practical/oral activity in the book and has no written answer. Fruits are the important part of plants and we like to eat fruits.

Q: Children! Can you tell which fruit has seeds? Fruits with seed: i. _____ ii. _____ iii. _____

Ans: There are seeds in most of the fruits. Three fruits with seeds shown in the book are: i. Apple ii. Mango iii. Watermelon.

Q: Activity (book p. 53): Celebrate plantation week in the school with the help of your teacher. The children bring plants, water their planted ones regularly and protect them.

Ans: Note: This is a practical/oral activity in the book and has no written answer.

Key Points

  • A plant needs light, water and air to grow well.
  • Carrot, radish, turnip and beetroot are roots that we eat.

lessons.title: End of Chapter Exercise
lessons.notes_html:
Parts of a Plant

  • The leaf makes the food of the plant with water, air and light.
  • The root remains inside the soil and keeps the plant holding inside the ground. It absorbs water from the ground and takes it to the stem.

Solved Questions and Answers

Q: Q1. Given below tick those vegetables which are the roots of plants. (Tomato, Carrot, Radish, Ginger, Turnip, Mint)

Ans: Tick Carrot, Radish and Turnip. These are the roots of plants that we eat. Tomato, ginger and mint are not ticked.

Q: Q2. Name the part given below and write its function. (Picture of a green leaf)

Ans: Name: Leaf. Function: The leaf makes the food of the plant with water, air and light.

Q: Q2. Name the part given below and write its function. (Picture of roots under the soil)

Ans: Name: Root. Function: The root remains inside the soil and keeps the plant holding inside the ground. It absorbs water from the ground and takes it to the stem.

Q: Q3. What will happen if there are no trees and plants around us? Tell any three drawbacks.

Ans: 1. The Earth's temperature will increase. 2. The air will not stay clean and the weather will not be pleasant. 3. Birds and animals will not get food, because trees produce food for the birds and animals.

Q: Q4. What are benefits of plants to us? Write any two benefits of plants.

Ans: i. The wood of trees is used for making houses and furniture. ii. Plants keep the air clean and make our environment beautiful.

Q: Q5. Name any three flowering plants.

Ans: i. Rose ii. Sunflower iii. Mango. Flowering plants have flowers and seeds in them.

Key Points

  • The leaf makes food for the plant; the root holds the plant and absorbs water.
  • Without trees, the temperature will increase and the air will not stay clean.

lessons.title: Where Animals Live
lessons.notes_html:
Animals and Their Homes

  • Land animals named in the book are camel, lion and elephant. Aquatic animals are shark, star fish and octopus.
  • The crocodile and the frog live both on land and in water.
  • The eagle lives in mountains, the rabbit in a burrow, the camel in the desert, the lion in a den, the sparrow in a nest and the dolphin in the ocean.

Animals and Their Babies

  • Babies named in the book: cat and kitten, hen and chicks, horse and foal, frog and tadpoles, butterfly and caterpillars.

Solved Questions and Answers

Q: Look at the given pictures carefully and fill the columns. Show the land animals with red colour. (Pictures on book pp. 55-56 include camel, lion and elephant)

Ans: Land animals: Camel, Lion and Elephant. These animals live on land.

Q: Show the aquatic animals with green colour. (Pictures on book p. 56 are Shark, Star Fish and Octopus)

Ans: Aquatic animals: Shark, Star Fish and Octopus. These animals live in water.

Q: Show by encircling with blue colour, the animals living both on land and in water. (Pictures on book p. 56 include a crocodile and a frog)

Ans: Animals living both on land and in water: Crocodile and Frog.

Q: Activity (book p. 57): Bring the pictures of different animals and their babies to the class and identify the babies of the animals.

Ans: Note: This is a practical/oral activity in the book and has no written answer. The babies named in the book are: cat and kitten, hen and chicks, horse and foal, frog and tadpoles, and butterfly and caterpillars.

Q: Tell about the animals around you, where do they live?

Ans: Animals live in different places. The eagle lives in mountains, the rabbit lives in a burrow, the camel lives in the desert, the lion lives in a den, the sparrow lives in a nest and the dolphin lives in the ocean.

Q: Activity (book p. 58): Make a chart. Paste the picture of your favourite animal and give the following information about it. (Picture, Name, Where lives, What eats, How many legs, Tail)

Ans: Note: This is a practical/oral activity in the book and has no written answer.

Key Points

  • Camel, lion and elephant live on land; shark, star fish and octopus live in water.
  • The crocodile and the frog live both on land and in water.

lessons.title: Crops of Pakistan
lessons.notes_html:
Crops and What They Give Us

  • The important crops of Pakistan named in the book are wheat, rice, cotton, sugarcane and maize.
  • Pulses used in our homes come from crops grown by farmers in the fields.
  • From cotton, thread is made; from thread, cloth is made; and from cloth, a dress is made.
  • Flour is made of wheat, and biscuits and bread are made from flour. Gur (jaggery) and sugar are made from the juice of sugarcane.

Solved Questions and Answers

Q: Activity (book p. 62): Bring the seeds of various crops to the class and ask your class mates which crops the seeds belong.

Ans: Note: This is a practical/oral activity in the book and has no written answer. The important crops of Pakistan named in the book are wheat, rice, cotton, sugarcane and maize.

Q: Activity (book p. 63): Think for a while: What is made from the crop of sunflower?

Ans: Note: This is a practical/oral activity in the book and has no written answer. The book's lesson text in this chapter does not name any product made from sunflower.

Q: Think for a while: From where we get the pulses used in our homes?

Ans: Pulses are crops. Farmers grow crops in the fields, and we get the pulses used in our homes from these crops.

Q: Activity (book p. 66): Complete the following given process by pasting pictures. (Cotton, Thread, Cloth, Dress)

Ans: Note: This is a practical pasting activity in the book and has no written answer. The process shown in the book is: thread is made from cotton, cloth is made from thread, and a dress is made from cloth, so pictures of thread, cloth and a dress are pasted in the empty circles in this order.

Key Points

  • Wheat, rice, cotton, sugarcane and maize are important crops of Pakistan.
  • Cotton makes thread, thread makes cloth and cloth makes a dress.

Ans: Three things we get from livestock are: (i) milk, (ii) meat, and (iii) leather. The book says buffalo and cow give milk, the meat of livestock is eaten, and the skin of livestock is used for making leather.

Q: Q3. Name any two important crops of Pakistan.

Ans: Two important crops of Pakistan are: (i) wheat, (ii) cotton. The book also names rice, sugarcane and maize as important crops of Pakistan.

lessons.title: The Importance of Forests
lessons.notes_html:
Why Forests Are Important

  • Forests are the place of living for animals and birds.
  • We get wood, furniture, paper and matches from forests.
  • Forests keep the weather pleasant and control soil erosion and flooding, so we should protect the trees.
  • To protect natural resources: avoid wood cutting without reason, use other sources of fuel instead of wood, keep the forests safe from fire, plant maximum trees, and use water carefully.

Solved Questions and Answers

Q: Children! What are the people doing in the picture? (Picture of people cutting trees in a forest)

Ans: The people in the picture are cutting trees in the forest. One man is carrying a saw and the others are cutting a tree.

Q: Are they doing the right things? If not why?

Ans: No, they are not doing the right thing. Forests are the place of living for animals and birds, and we get wood, furniture, paper and matches from forests. Forests keep the weather pleasant and control soil erosion and flooding, so we should protect the trees and save them from wasting.

Q: Activity (book p. 73): Make poster in group and tell that how can we protect the natural resources.

Ans: Note: This is a practical group activity in the book and has no written answer. The book tells these ways to protect natural resources: avoid wood cutting without reason, use other sources of fuel instead of wood, keep the forests safe from fire, plant maximum trees, and use water carefully and not waste it.

Key Points

  • Forests are the home of animals and birds and give us wood, furniture, paper and matches.
  • We should plant more trees and protect forests from cutting and fire.

lessons.title: Sources of Heat and Light
lessons.notes_html:
Heat and Light Around Us

  • When we rub our hands for a bit longer, our hands become warm, because heat is produced by rubbing. Long ago, man discovered fire by rubbing the stones.
  • Natural sources of heat and light are the sun, the moon and the stars.
  • Artificial (man-made) sources are burning wood, candle, gas and electricity.
  • The intensity of heat and light is felt more as we come nearer to the source.

Solved Questions and Answers

Q: Activity (book p. 76): Rub both your hands and observe that what happens when rubbing continues a bit longer.

Ans: Note: This is a practical activity in the book and has no written answer. When we rub our hands for a bit longer, our hands become warm, because heat is produced by rubbing. The book also tells that man in old times discovered fire by rubbing the stones.

Q: Activity (book p. 78): Divide the children in two groups. Every group should visit their school. One group make the list of natural sources of heat and light, whereas the other group make the list of artificial sources, and present it in the class.

Ans: Note: This is a practical group activity in the book and has no written answer. From the book, natural sources are the sun, the moon and the stars, and artificial (man-made) sources are burning wood, candle, gas and electricity.

Q: Look at the pictures given below and tell that where more light and heat is reaching and why? (Pictures of a girl holding a torch near and far from an object, and a boy sitting near and far from a fireplace)

Ans: More light and heat reaches at the nearer place. The book's learning outcomes say that the intensity of heat and light is felt more as we come nearer to the source, so the object near the torch gets more light and the boy near the fireplace feels more heat.

Key Points

  • Heat is produced by rubbing; the sun, moon and stars are natural sources of light.
  • Heat and light are felt more when we are near to the source.

Ans: False — a furnace or heater gives more heat to the one who is near it, because heat is felt more nearer to the source.

Ans: Natural Source. The book says the sun is the natural and biggest source of heat and light.

  • The sun is the natural and biggest source of heat and light.

The Story of Sara and Nida

  • Sara forgave Nida, and they became good friends again. Forgiveness is a good quality.

Solved Questions and Answers

Q: Did Nida behave nicely with Sara in the class on first day?

Ans: No, Nida did not behave nicely with Sara on the first day. She called Sara with bad names and laughed at her, so Sara became very sad and could not study all the day.

Q: What would you do if you were instead of Sara?

Ans: If I were instead of Sara, I would also forgive my friend like Sara did. I would help her in her need, because forgiveness is a good quality.

Q: Have you ever pardoned someone on mistake? How did you feel after the pardon?

Ans: Yes, I have pardoned my friend on his mistake. After the pardon I felt happy and light, and we became good friends again, just as Sara and Nida became good friends.

Q: Write the benefits of forbearance.

Ans: The benefits of forbearance are: (1) Forgiveness is a good quality and it makes good friends. (2) It ends sadness and fighting. (3) People who are pardoned feel ashamed of their bad behaviour and become good. (4) We should not hurt anyone, and if someone hurts us, it is better to pardon.

Key Points

  • Forgiveness makes good friends and ends sadness and fighting.
  • After pardoning someone, we feel happy and light.

lessons.title: End of Chapter Exercise
lessons.notes_html:
The Lion, the Monkey and the Elephant

  • The bear and the pigeon told the truth to the lion, so the lion could do justice and the monkey got his right.
  • The elephant had teased the monkey and told lies, so he had to serve the monkey for one month and collect fruits for him. The lesson of the story is that justice and impartiality should always be maintained.

Solved Questions and Answers

Q: True/False: Behaving nicely with others is a good habit.

Ans: True

Q: True/False: Taking more than your share is bad act.

Ans: True

Q: True/False: He who does not accept his mistake is a great man.

Ans: False — we should accept our mistake, as the elephant accepted his mistake in the story.

Q: True/False: We should adopt justice-loving in life

Ans: True

Q: Did bear and pigeon do the right thing by telling the truth to the lion. Why?

Ans: Yes, the bear and the pigeon did the right thing by telling the truth to the lion. Because of their truth, the lion could do justice and the monkey got his right.

Q: What decision would you give for the elephant if you were instead of the lion?

Ans: If I were instead of the lion, I would give the same just decision. The elephant would serve the monkey for one month and collect fruits for him, because he teased the monkey and also told lies.

Q: Activity (book p. 100): Q4. What lesson did you derive from the story? Tell orally.

Ans: Note: This is an oral activity in the book and has no written answer. The lesson given in the book is: We get the lesson from this story that justice and impartiality always be maintained.

Key Points

  • Always tell the truth and accept your mistake.
  • Justice and impartiality should always be maintained.
